$comment: Hard limits, in BROTLI-compressed bytes, enforced by scripts/check-budgets.mjs on every build. These are set close to current reality on purpose — a budget with 4x headroom enforces nothing. Raising a number is a deliberate decision that shows up in a diff, which is the whole point: 'no exceptions' only survives if a machine enforces it. LOWERING one matters just as much and is far easier to forget, which is what `ratchet` is for: `npm run budgets:ratchet` pulls every number back down to what the bundle actually weighs today. `data` covers any `data-*` manualChunk — a STATIC TABLE rather than a page (today: data-seasonality, the almanac's encoded year curves and event date tables). It is separate from `route` on purpose: folding a 300KB table into the page budget would mean raising `route` to ~130kb, and a route budget with that much headroom stops enforcing anything for the twelve pages that carry no table at all. Its 78000 is a FIRST number, taken from the brotli weight of the SOURCES before the chunk had ever been built — ratchet it after the first real build.
$raised: 2026-09-17 — entry 38900 -> 44000, css 8500 -> 9000. NOT a workaround; the shell genuinely grew. What landed since these numbers were last set: the alerts feed (shell/AlertsFeed.tsx + alertTypes.ts, both eager because AlertsPill is always on the toolbar and its headline comes from toItem()), and CopyShot. Before raising, every panel in the entry was checked for a missed split and all of them were already lazy: AlertsPanel, BzilaPanel, BotAlertPanel, NotesDock, NoteClipMenu, and snapshot.ts behind a dynamic import inside useShot. THE ONE SPLIT STILL ON THE TABLE is CopyShotMenu — a click-to-open surface sitting in the same module as CopyShotProvider, so Rollup cannot split it where it is. Moving it to its own file (and with it the menu-only helpers: useShot, claimClipboard, slug, GLYPH, TONE, loadOrder/saveOrder, rankOf) should give a few kb back; ratchet these numbers down when it lands. Headroom here is ~2% on purpose - enough that a comment does not fail a build, tight enough to still enforce. NOTE the deploy never sees this check: the root Dockerfile runs `build:fast` (plain vite build), deliberately, so an over-budget v3 cannot cost the site a hotfix. That makes this a COMMIT-time gate only, and it had not been run since the shell work landed - which is why v9.16.19 shipped green while local was 4.1kb over.

ratchet.$comment: slack = how much headroom a budget may carry before it stops enforcing anything. When the largest asset of a kind is more than this fraction under its budget, the check reports SLACK. enforce=true turns those reports into build failures; leave it false so a bundle getting SMALLER never blocks a commit — re-tighten deliberately with `npm run budgets:ratchet`.

perf.$comment: Limits for scripts/perf-check.mjs, which counts REPAINTS PER ANIMATION FRAME on every canvas v3 owns (the ones tagged data-cb-layer), attributed per board card. idleRepaintsPerFrame is measured with the card on screen and nothing happening — not zero, because a live spot legitimately moves the price mapping and the pane autoscales with it. offscreenRepaints is a hard zero: a card scrolled out of view must not paint at all. interactionRepaints is the other half of the guard — a gate that suppressed everything would pass every other line here.
